page_title: Write You a Haskell ( Stephen Diehl )

summary.title: Write You a Haskell
summary.one_liner: A project-based tutorial for building a small lazy functional language, Fun, a partial Haskell 2010 subset, from parser through type inference to native code generation.
takeaways: How to design and implement a small functional language called Fun, a partial Haskell 2010 subset
How parsing, renaming, pattern matching desugaring and Hindley-Milner type inference fit together
How typeclasses, higher-kinded types and System-F style polymorphism are implemented
How Core, STG and lazy evaluation lead to an interpreter and native code generation via C or LLVM
The text is a pre-edited rough cut of the chapters, which the author planned to refine over time
summary.summary: This is the landing page for Stephen Diehl's project-based tutorial on building a functional language called Fun, a partial Haskell 2010 toy language. The page introduces the goal of covering engineering details that most language resources skip, and lists 28 chapters. The chapters progress from Haskell basics, parsing and lambda calculus through type systems and Hindley-Milner inference, to Core, STG, an interpreter, a runtime, and code generation via C and LLVM. The page is a rough, unedited draft, and the license is Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 4.0 for text and MIT for source.
